title: Phase-coordinated multi-GPU handoff planner for prefill and decode
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We see recurring latency spikes at the boundaries between prefill and decode when serving long-context generations on tensor+pipeline parallel configurations. Those spikes correlate with sudden NCCL allreduce/allgather bursts and runtime kernel switching for attention (FP16->quantized paths).

Problem: The serving runtime's current handoff is reactive: compute stages signal availability and the conductor schedules the next microbatch. With heterogeneous device bandwidth and variable token lengths, this leads to contention windows where many stages simultaneously initiate communication and expensive attention kernels, causing 95th+ latency regressions and tail jitter.

Goal: Implement a phase-coordinated handoff planner that: 1) assigns fine-grained phase windows for prefill vs decode handoffs across tensor/pipeline stages, 2) emits lightweight kernel selection hints ahead of handoff to pre-warm kernels and memory paths, and 3) staggers NCCL rendezvous within bounded watermarks to preserve SLOs while minimizing throughput loss.

Success metrics: 
- Reduce end-to-end 95th-percentile latency for long-context prefill+decode workloads by >=15% on heterogeneous 8-GPU pools.
- Keep median throughput within 3% of current baseline.
- No increase in OOM incidents or memory tail events.

Constraints and non-goals: 
- This ticket focuses on runtime planner logic and kernel hint API; it does not change kernel implementations or introduce new NCCL primitives.
- Will be opt-in behind a runtime flag and limited to supported topologies (tensor parallelism with pipeline stages >=2).

Proposal summary: 
1) Phase window allocator: maintain moving watermarks per-request representing prefill and decode phases. Allocate adjustable micro-windows (e.g., 1-4ms) that each stage can reserve for handoffs. The allocator enforces max concurrent rendezvous to smooth NCCL traffic.
2) Kernel hint channel: a 16-byte compact hint sent 1-2 micro-windows before a handoff containing (a) expected attention type (dense/sparse/flash), (b) quantization bucket, and (c) estimated sequence-length delta. Runtime uses hints to pre-select kernels and warm caches.
3) Staggered rendezvous policy: use topology-aware backoffs (based on measured device bandwidth + observed NCCL latencies) to compute per-stage offsets.
4) Telemetry: add new tags to per-request traces: planned_phase_window, actual_handoff_offset_ms, kernel_hint_used, nccl_spike_flag. Link these to Console dashboards and alerts for regression detection.

Deliverables: 
- Planner core in runtime (C++), with config flags and a lightweight hint protocol.
- Runtime unit tests and integration harness for 4-GPU and 8-GPU emulations.
- Perf harness runs, dashboards, and a /playground experiment template for QA.
- Doc page for the kernel hint spec and opt-in rollout instructions.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Planner toggled on shows >=10% P95 improvement in internal perf runs for at least two representative long-context models (e.g., LlamaX-13B, Red-Base-7B) on heterogeneous clusters.
- Kernel hint path does not increase scheduling CPU overhead beyond 2% in steady-state.
- No regressions in 50th-percentile latency or memory safety tests.

Risks and mitigation: 
- Incorrect hinting could cause worse kernel choices: mitigation -> canary rollout + fallback to existing kernel selector when hints are missing/confident=false.
- Watermark calibration complexity on very bursty workloads: mitigation -> expose tuning knobs (max_concurrent_rendezvous, window_ms) and auto-calibration mode that uses short-running probes.

Related artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Phase+Handoff+Planner, perf dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/phase-handoff-experiments, design sketch: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1phase-sketch, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824
comments: 2026-02-12 - Asha Patel: Initial triage. Observed correlated NCCL peaks when toggling flash-attn paths and with variable prefill lengths. Created design doc and sketched allocator API. Added Diego to assignee.

2026-02-18 - Diego Morales: Spike done — micro-emulation harness for 4-GPU topologies implemented. Early results show reduced NCCL concurrency but kernel warmup increased 50-100us per handoff. Need to measure end-to-end impact on P95.
2026-02-24 - Diego Morales: RFC posted in #runtime-arch. Key trade-off: larger windows smooth NCCL but increase latency scheduling contention. Proposal to start with 2ms windows and auto-tune.
2026-02-28 - PM review (Nina Wu): Please include canary rollout steps and a telemetry plan to alert on regressions for enterprise customers. Added to deliverables.
2026-03-03 - Eng review (Ravi Singh): Code-level feedback on hint encoding — prefer compact uint8 flags to minimize serialization overhead. Raised PR comment on prototype PR.

2026-03-05 - Diego Morales: Benchmark update: with 8-GPU heterogeneous cluster (A100 + A10 mix) and LlamaX-13B, enabling planner with conservative offsets yielded 12% P95 improvement and 2% throughput drop. Still under target; will try topology-aware offsets next. Perf data linked in dashboard.

2026-03-08 - Diego Morales: PR 1824 updated with kernel hint compact encoding, and fallback gate when hint confidence <0.6. Added integration test which simulates missing hints. CI flaky on one test related to simulated NCCL latency — investigating.

2026-03-10 - Asha Patel: Design review meeting notes: decided to expose tuning knobs via runtime config and Console UI. Action items: Diego to stabilize PR and add telemetry tags; Observability team (Ruth) to add dashboard widgets for actual_handoff_offset_ms.
